outcome: Incidence of cumulative Bishop score increases ≥3 within 12 hours
Incidence of vaginal delivery within 24 hours
cohort: 222 nulliparous women at term pregnancy in China
finding: Intravaginal misoprostol (25 μg every 4 hours) was found to be efficacious and safe for labor induction and cervical ripening in nulliparous women at term pregnancy, leading to a higher incidence of Bishop score increases and vaginal delivery within 24 hours, and a shorter induction-onset of labor interval, without significant differences in adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Although misoprostol led to a higher incidence of labor induction, there were no significant differences in the incidence of cesarean section deliveries between the misoprostol and placebo groups.
